newsitem.title: USA: Florida Aquarium president cuts own job.
newsitem.headline: Florida Aquarium president cuts own job.

text.p: The president and chief executive officer of the troubled Florida Aquarium has eliminated four top jobs, including his own, to cut costs.
Aquarium President, John Racanelli, announced the cuts in a news conference Monday.
He said they would save the city-owned aquarium $260,000 a year without depriving the aquarium of "the people who do the heavy lifting."
In addition to his $120,000-a-year post, Racanelli eliminated two vice presidents' posts and the director of human resources' job, effective in June and August.
In their place, the aquarium will create a new position of general manager to oversee five managers who used to report to the vice presidents or to Racanelli.
One-third of the aquarium's staff was laid off or demoted in January, reducing the staff to 104, in order to stave off $2 million of operating losses.
The nonprofit aquarium opened in 1995 but has failed to attract enough visitors to pay debt service on its bonds.
The City of Tampa assumed ownership of the facility in October and issued $104 million of revenue bonds to refinance the debt.
